posq9Yes.answer: I thought the high school grad rate in California being the lowest in the country was interesting. The inconsistency of wiki pages was too.

post10-sbert.answer: The flow of the summaries seemed better. I mean if I just read a summary without thinking about what input I had put in, then V put out a nice concise summary for some of the states. Even if it disregarded my input.

post11-sbert.answer: It didn't have the sliders to increase focus. I had to go back and add states, but that didn't seem to help.

post3Yes-sbert.answer: The summaries didn't really have what I wanted in them. I went and added another state. It didn't seem to change the output.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: I mean they kind of were in some ways ok. The overall summaries were good, but they didn't really seem to use my inputs. I got a summary that gave me an impression of a state, but without my specific areas of focus.

post9-sbert.answer: It just had the politics and coastal location. It had state income tax, but not high like California or NY.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: It just spit out the few things I'm interested in when I start a search like this. It gives me a quick way to eliminate places I don't want to live in vs ones I may focus on more closely.

post12-sudocu.answer: I lived in Washington so I know what is there. I figured it would be easy to feed information to the AI if I already knew a state had what I wanted. The wiki for states like Washington is a little more civilized than say Alabama.

post13-sudocu.answer: It was simple. The sliders and buttons had hover over names so I could quickly figure out what is what. The AI seemed to work adequately.

post14-sudocu.answer: Not really anything. I seemed to work as intended. I think the weaknesses lie more in Wikipedia and the variance in quality of pages.

post3Yes-sudocu.answer: They were ok, but I wanted more focus on weather and taxes. State income tax. It seemed to work.

post6Yes1-sudocu.answer: I moved the 2 areas I wanted more focus on all the way over to the right. I didn't move any of the others down.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: It seemed easier to see what I wanted to see in the summaries. That could be that I was looking a second time, but the summaries on my second look seemed more focused on what I needed.

preq1.answer: Usually to find a solution to a problem. For example, I am rebuilding my late 90's mountain bike. I have to get a part off and clean it. Then search online to find what that part is from catalogs of the late 90's or whatever. Then I start searching for modern replacements or direct replacements. If not available I search forums for workarounds.

preq3.answer: I use multiple search engines. Some forums or different contemporary sources.

preq5.answer: I start broad to see what I have to work with then go more and more specific.

posq9Yes.answer: When I started the first round of the task, I read through a few of the entries to get an idea of the kind of information available in each entry, which helped me identify attributes that were important to me that I might not have remembered off the top of my head.

post10-sbert.answer: It didn't seem to require too much input in order to generate summaries that captured the details I was most interested in, which made it easier to review the information and make a decision. Selecting sentences itself was also easy, and generation of summaries was very fast.

post11-sbert.answer: The presentation of Wikipedia information was very bare-bones. Being able to jump to sections would have been a huge help, instead of having to pick through everything just to find the details I want with nothing to break apart the giant block of text. This was easily the most frustrating part of the experience. And while the search function helped a bit, it also isolated only parts containing the search term, so that related sentences occurring before and afterwards which might have had important information were not available as long as the search term was entered. In the end, it was much easier to use my browser's search function to scroll through instances of the search term in the whole document, but again, some basic formatting would have helped a great deal, even just paragraph breaks. In addition, quite a bit of information on Wikipedia is also tabular or list-based, or presented as graphics, and none of this seemed to be available. Finally, not being able to adjust the size of the text windows was also very annoying, making it much harder to scan for interesting details.

post13-sbert.answer: I would not be interested in using this system unless I was able to use it directly on the actual Wikipedia page or a copy that closely approximates its formatting and navigability. Given that Wiki pages on the same topics generally have the same elements, it would also be much easier for an end-user to identify categories of information they are interested in, like demographics, economy, climate, etc., rather than have to pick these elements out of the text themselves. In the time it took to do just a few of these manually, I could have already found comparisons of the elements I was interested in elsewhere online.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: The summaries generally contained the details I was primarily interested in: weather/climate, geography, transit, and natural points of interest, so it was somewhat easy to compare.

post8Yes-sbert.answer: Only in a small number of generated summaries was there information I had not included in any of the summaries I compiled manually, related to politics and/or demographics. I don't believe I selected any such information when making my initial manual summaries.

post9-sbert.answer: I chose California primarily due to the variety of weather, especially the abundance of warm/hot regions, and variety of geography in the state, and also its location next to an ocean. Secondary reasons include an extensive education system and abundance of mass transit options. I've actually lived in many states, especially in the northeast of the US, and am currently living in the midwest, so that also helped rule out a lot of places as I'd much rather experience somewhere new.

post12-sudocu.answer: I chose North Carolina based on its proximity to the ocean, reasonably warm climate, and my interest in its ecological characteristics. Of secondary interest was its extensive state education system.

post13-sudocu.answer: In theory, I like the idea of dynamically composed keyword groupings that can be assigned a particular weight, but I'm not sold on this particular implementation.

post14-sudocu.answer: I don't want to repeat everything I wrote in my first response about System V, but all of those criticisms are applicable here as well. In addition, I would add that the slider system seems to pull in some keywords like institution, city and state names that should probably not be included, as they are less likely to be relevant to other states. I felt like I got longer generated summaries that had substantially more 'false positives', i.e. information I did not ask for.

post16-sudocu.answer: One thing I forgot to note before but this applies to both systems: there appear to be parsing errors, most likely where paragraphs end. For some sentences, there is no space following the period at its end, so the sentence highlighting system treats this and the following sentence as connected, and these can contain very different subject matter. As there is no way to split these sentences, the user's only choice is to either leave out a sentence which may be important, or include it with the additional sentence which may contain information they are not interested in. This may be a source of the 'false positives' that users may experience.

posq9Yes.answer: It helped me to think of more things that were of interest to me and therefore more keywords I could search to update the summaries.

post10-sbert.answer: It was very simple and easy to use and navigate.

post11-sbert.answer: It was also extremely slow and it would take a while for my keywords to generate summaries. I noticed it didn't have the sliders, which would have been nice to try had they worked.

post3Yes-sbert.answer: As I read the summaries for different states, I found keywords that were of interest to me and so I went back in to the example inputs and updated the summaries.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: The summaries provided a good understanding as to what things were located in each state that were of interest to me.

post8Yes-sbert.answer: Sometimes there was information included that had nothing to do with what I was searching for, such as information about banks and cities within the state.

post9-sbert.answer: Because it has plenty of mountain and scenic wilderness areas that could be hiked and explored, which is something I love to do.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: They gave information on whether the state had the things that were of interest to me.

post12-sudocu.answer: It has many national parks and natural areas that could be used for hiking and enjoying the outdoors, which is a huge interest of mine.

post13-sudocu.answer: It was easy to navigate and use.

post14-sudocu.answer: It was very slow and lagged. The sliders did not work.

post3No-sudocu.answer: I felt there was enough information.

post6No-sudocu.answer: I tried to use them and they would not move at all.

preq1.answer: To find the most efficient answer or information I am looking for.

post13-sudocu.answer: It simplified things somewhat. It was fairly easy to use. I think it would be useful if it allowed for searching in a broader variety of websites.

post14-sudocu.answer: I couldn't add anything into the summary that wasn't in the article. I couldn't find anything about housing or cost of living or public transportation, all of which are important in considering a state. posq10.answer: I feel like I was more comfortable with the system overall by the time I got to system V. Perhaps this could introduce some bias. I spent a lot of time with system U figuring it out. By the time I moved onto System V I knew exactly what I was supposed to be doing. I had a better idea about what I should be doing and how things worked. Both were somewhat similar overall.

post10-sbert.answer: I liked that it relied on searching. I felt like I was able to very quickly find relevant information this way.

post11-sbert.answer: The searching was a little slow to load at times. I would type and it would get hung up for a few seconds.

post3No-sbert.answer: I didn't feel the need.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: They provided brief summaries with only information I found relevant.

post9-sbert.answer: I liked the fact that most people in the state lived in urban areas.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: They streamlined the massive amount of information provided for each state.

post11Yes-sudocu.answer: A lot of it was historical information. I wasn't expecting history. I was expecting general statistical information.

post12-sudocu.answer: I knew a little bit about the state beforehand. I guess I was biased. But the information I read about the state made me like it even more.

post13-sudocu.answer: I liked that there was a lot of information on the screen at once. And this information was presented in a very organized way. I felt like most of the interface was easy to understand with intuitive controls. I liked the self-highlighting.

post14-sudocu.answer: I didn't like the slider section. I couldn't figure out how it worked.

post3No-sudocu.answer: I wasn't sure why it was necessary.

post6No-sudocu.answer: I couldn't figure out how to move the sliders.

preq1.answer: My goal is to find the most relevant information as quickly as possible. I want to be efficient. This means spending a sufficient amount of time per search. This also means focusing on results which are highly relevant and contain the most useful information.

preq3.answer: I use online search engines mostly. Sometimes I will search forums or social media sites like reddit.

preq5.answer: I would say I generally have some go to sites besides the obvious (Google) which I stick to. These might be sites or references that I've used in the past and know are legit and trustworthy.

posq10.answer: I think System V is overall easier and it generated summaries that were really good considering how easy it is to use. But if I wasn't already knowledgeable about various states, and was researching a topic I know nothing about, I'd choose System U because the sliders help me figure out where to even start summarizing and what keywords exist to be honed in on

post10-sbert.answer: The summaries were very comprehensive and easy to read

post11-sbert.answer: I missed having the sliders from the first system! Those were useful for easily and quickly modifying the generated summaries

post3No-sbert.answer: I didn't feel like I needed to

post7Yes-sbert.answer: They had exactly the content I wanted them to have, I was impressed with how well they were able to create little snapshots of what I want to know about a state

post9-sbert.answer: Economic/climate concerns are always my #1 interest, with a third concern being how family-friendly the state is (so Utah would be my pick probably)

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: By emphasizing the economic and climate factors that would lead me to select a state

post12-sudocu.answer: N/A

post13-sudocu.answer: It was actually really fun to read up on these states, generate summaries and toy around with automatically customizing summaries

post14-sudocu.answer: I really really hated that each state I was doing input summaries for was just A HUGE block of text with no paragraph breaks, which made it very difficult to read and parse the way I needed to do it to make my own initial summaries

post3Yes-sudocu.answer: To fit what I thought a good summary should look like

post6Yes1-sudocu.answer: because I felt like they had too many keywords specific to the input summaries that didn't apply to remaining states. for example my input summaries turned out to be of states with very heavy Hispanic ancestry/history that doesn't necessarily apply to all states, so I toned that keyword down.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: I just saw less emphasis and more on present day stats

preq1.answer: knowledge acquisition

preq5.answer: I try to skip over SEO spam, which is more and more frequent on Google nowadays. I prefer to read forums/reddit first to get a feel for how other people feel about the information. sometimes I only search using the search operator site:.edu so I only see websites that are more credible.

posq10.answer: System U did a lot better in terms or pulling up search terms with a partial input. For example I could type "tax" and it would include "taxes" as well. System V did not perform in this manner which made it harder to find information.

posq9Yes.answer: Coming across this new information helped me to think of more keywords to search.

post10-sbert.answer: System seemed smoother when moving between generated summaries. A bit more responsive than the other system.

post11-sbert.answer: The generated summaries seemed low quality and did not present enough information. Estimate they were 1/4 of my example in length.

post13-sbert.answer: The other system was better even with the system lag.

post3Yes-sbert.answer: Forgot to select certain information for states so went back and did that.

post7No-sbert.answer: The generated summaries did not have enough information in them despite me selecting a lot in my examples. Relied on the information I found myself more so than the generated info.

post9-sbert.answer: I felt like Florida has the best situation relative to income tax/earnings. A lot of natural areas to explore as well as nice weather. A lot of high quality colleges.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: I was able to filter through the information faster than if I had to read the entire page/search for the information myself.

post12-sudocu.answer: I liked the history of the state, the sports teams, politics and school systems. There is also a lot of nature to explore.

post13-sudocu.answer: Easy to filter through information and get summaries curated to my search. The weighting system was useful as well.

post14-sudocu.answer: After using the system for a bit I noticed the lag increase when generating summaries. Thought it froze completely a few times.

post16-sudocu.answer: If there were no system lag it would be a perfect tool for me to use. Have a pretty good gaming PC so do not think the lag was on my end.

post3Yes-sudocu.answer: I wanted more information for the system to use after thinking of another search term.

post6Yes1-sudocu.answer: I wanted to see more information on the state's nature/natural wonders, sports, colleges, and tax information compared to the rest.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: More focus on the topics specified though it was not a huge change.

preq1.answer: Knowledge acquisition for the most part. Sometimes it is work based and other times are personal interests. I use this behavior for purchasing decisions as well when comparing product lists/reviews for a category that I am purchasing in.

preq3.answer: Online search engines for the most part though I have started to use AI chatbots for the initial search process.

preq5.answer: Usually I will compile a list of resources in a wordpad or other note taking software as I come across what I feel is high quality information. Utilizing multiple search engines at times.

post9-sbert.answer: It fit what I was looking for. It's liberal and ranks high for life expectancy and low unemployment. I like the national parks/tree/coast/mountains/lakes.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: The tax information it gave me was pretty useful and actually helped me eliminate a state I thought I wanted to live in.

post12-sudocu.answer: My main criteria was a liberal state, good weather, coast, trees, good economy and low taxes. This state met most of these requirements.

post13-sudocu.answer: I really like the idea of the slider system and being able to influence which topics the summaries are about.

post14-sudocu.answer: I felt the keywords were a bit all over the place could be simpler or just a few words.

post16-sudocu.answer: Umm the first question needs 3 states to move on... I only used 2 which was Okay according to the directions.  I used way more than two in the first set and wanted to do less on this one. Anyways I had to pick a random state to move on(Wisconsin).

post3Yes-sudocu.answer: i just wanted to add a bit more to them to help get a more accurate summary later.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: I'm not sure to be honest but it did seem as if it put more emphasis on certain topics.

preq5.answer: I have no strategy.

posq9Yes.answer: It caught my eye and gave me information I had not considered looking up and then more detailed information than I expected.  More information certainly helps.  More the better to make decisions.

post10-sbert.answer: I liked how it was easy to type in text to filter out what I am looking for.  It really cuts down my time in searching and reading.  I really hate reading information that is not relevant to me.  Allows me to go straight to the information I need.

post11-sbert.answer: There were some keywords that wouldn't search anything for me.  It is probably not in there so it wasn't able to bring it up for me.  There were some information that I felt was missing.  Florida as far as I know does not have state taxes.  Information on there is bit old and outdated.  Florida's governor isn't Rick Scott anymore, that much I know.  If I wanted to search Ron DeSantis, it wouldn't come up anything.  It also loads slowly so I am waiting for my keyword search to show up then find out there's nothing or it's just slow to load.

post13-sbert.answer: I liked it very much, just needs to be updated.

post3Yes-sbert.answer: I wanted it to summarize the information I wanted and not the extras that I was not interested in.  There were some I wanted to remove.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: I liked the information that was brief and summarized for me so I could look at it by glance without having to look at a wall of text which would be overwhelming to me.  I only picked out the main points of each state that were of interest to me.

post9-sbert.answer: I had an interest in these states and have wanted to move there.  I love warm weather so I wanted Arizona along with Texas to compare with Florida.  I felt that they all were states I was interested in previously then I selected a state that was bit different in location and weather.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: It highlighted what was more important to me so I can look at it first such as the weather.  Weather means a lot to me so I chose it as the important topic to me.

post12-sudocu.answer: It felt like a great state to live in.  It is an individual state that has no connection to the other states.  Seemed like a good choice based on the summaries that were of interest to me.

post13-sudocu.answer: I liked that the system U had topic importance because that helps me priorize what I feel is important or of interest to me over the other topics.  Going down to order of importance from top to bottom.  Screening out ones that aren't too important to me.

post14-sudocu.answer: I don't think there was anything that I disliked.  I was thinking that if I don't like it, I can just not use it and the system would be just fine.  Either use it or don't use it.  Definitely doesn't hurt to have it there if needed but it can easily be not in use.  It also could use more coloring I think to make it more pleasing to the eyes.

post3No-sudocu.answer: I selected what I wanted to select.  I didn't see the need to modify them at that point.  I did modify in the past but not in this set.

post6Yes1-sudocu.answer: I slid what I thought was more important to me such as the weather which helps highlight the summaries.  Ones that I didn't care for, I reduced it.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: When I changed it, I saw the generated summary highlight some of the words and bring it up to the top which showed that it was more important to me.

preq1.answer: Usually when I'm searching multiple websites, my goal is that I am looking for consistent information.  It feels like I can't rely on just one website or source.  I need to look for more of them and the more they are consistent, the more I believe it.  It validates the accuracy of the information.  I also like to read different ways of the same topic in how it's explained or said.  Some may be easier than others to understand.

preq3.answer: I use Google, the online search engine.  I'll go in then look for reliable websites that are trustworthy.

preq5.answer: There are keywords that I am looking for usually.  Sometimes I will type it in different way to search for information and see if anything new comes up after the first try.  Keywords are important in what I am looking for.

post10-sbert.answer: I liked how easy it was to use and that it was able to pull a lot of what I was looking for.

post11-sbert.answer: It had a harder time determining what kind of information I wanted about education. I think this was partially due to the inconsistency in the Wikipedia pages...not all of them listed educational information the same way.

post3Yes-sbert.answer: As I was working on the different states, I would add something new to one and then want to add it to the rest to compare that as well.

post7Yes-sbert.answer: It was easy to see just the things that were most important to me without the entire Wikipedia page in front of me. Having such detail is nice, but it can be overwhelming. I was able to read the summaries and say, "Oh, that doesn't sound good. I'm going to avoid that." or "Awesome! I am going to continue learning more about this state."

post9-sbert.answer: It has the best combination of my preferred political atmosphere, climate, and educational opportunities. I felt like I would be comfortable there.

post10Yes-sudocu.answer: I could see the things most important to me quickly without having to hunt in the page. Being able to switch between the states quickly meant I could see almost instantly how those states compared to each other.

post12-sudocu.answer: It would be the most comfortable for my family in terms of politics, religion, and education. I could tell pretty quickly which state was the most open.

post13-sudocu.answer: I absolutely loved the sliders. Being able to rank what is most important to me instead of the system trying to guess is great.

post14-sudocu.answer: There isn't anything I disliked about it.

post3Yes-sudocu.answer: Just to fine-tune them. I wanted to drill down a little bit more to see if I could get more of what I was looking for.

post6Yes1-sudocu.answer: I changed the sliders for my top three topics to give me better results. I left the rest alone since they aren't as important and wouldn't sway me one way or the other.

post6Yes2Yes-sudocu.answer: I think it might have changed the order of the summary sentences so the most important showed up first for me.

preq1.answer: I'm usually trying to find reviews about whatever product, location, or website I am interested in using to see what others have experienced with it. I want to try to avoid common problems.

preq3.answer: I typically only use search engines. I wouldn't know how to access a database for this.

preq5.answer: My strategy is usually to look for both positive and negative statements to try to determine whether there are commonalities and to make sure that the things I find are not just one-off successes or problems.
